cases.sentence: Я остался на площадке, в ___ и полном недоумении.
cases.explain: «полном одиночестве» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: I remained where I was, in complete loneliness and complete bewilderment. No, not quite bewilderment, but the same alarm turning into bitterness. Then, too, the hell with it—let it be "sweet vagabond"’ and "First Lieuten- ant," but why is it dark outside, tell me, please? Why is it dark outside if the train left in the morning and has gone exactly one hundred kilometers? Why?

cases.sentence: В конце концов, черт с ним, пусть «милая странница», пусть «___», – но почему за окном темно, скажите мне, пожалуйста?
cases.explain: «старший лейтенант» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: I remained where I was, in complete loneliness and complete bewilderment. No, not quite bewilderment, but the same alarm turning into bitterness. Then, too, the hell with it—let it be "sweet vagabond"’ and "First Lieuten- ant," but why is it dark outside, tell me, please? Why is it dark outside if the train left in the morning and has gone exactly one hundred kilometers? Why?

cases.sentence: Это ты! – кто-то сказал у меня за спиной таким ___, таким злорадным, что я даже поворачиваться не стал.
cases.explain: «приятным голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "Oh, that’s you," someone said from behind my back, in such a pleasant and malicious voice that I didn’t even need to turn around. I understood at once who was standing there behind me. "He’ll try to tempt me now, the stoneface. He’s been waiting for the right time to tempt me!"

cases.explain: «тупая морда» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "Oh, that’s you," someone said from behind my back, in such a pleasant and malicious voice that I didn’t even need to turn around. I understood at once who was standing there behind me. "He’ll try to tempt me now, the stoneface. He’s been waiting for the right time to tempt me!"

cases.explain: «духовный порыв» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: ‘Well, if it’s tough,’ Satan went on, "subdue your transport. Subdue your spiritual transport and it'll be easier."’

cases.sentence: С ___ бытия нам, дуракам, не совладать.
cases.explain: «извечными законами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "So what don’t you like about the dark? Dark is dark, and you can’t do anything about it. Dark is followed by light and light is followed by dark—that’s my opinion. And if you don’t like it, the dark won't cease to be dark just because of that. So there remains only one way out: accept the dark. It’s not for us fools to get the better of nature’s laws. Having stopped up our left nostril we can blow our nose only with the right one. Isn’t that so? Well, then, there’s no demanding light beyond the window if beyond the window it is dark.

cases.explain: «Курского вокзала» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "Yeah that’s true. . . but, you know, I did leave in the morning. At eight-sixteen, from the Kursk Station."’

cases.explain: «прошлая пятница» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "What’s last Friday got to do with it? Who cares about last Friday! Last Friday the train hardly made any stops. And, in general, trains traveled faster then, but now, the devil knows, they stop and wait. For what? It’s enough to make you sick sometimes. Why is it always stopping? Like that at every marker. Except Esino."’ I glanced out the window and frowned again.

cases.sentence: Как обидно, что я на ___ еду к ней совершенно трезвый.
cases.explain: «тринадцатый раз» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: And suddenly jumped up from my place. "Gracious Lord! But she’s supposed to be waiting for me at eleven in the morning. At eleven she’s supposed to be waiting for me and outside it’s still dark. So, I'll have to wait for her until morning. I don’t really know where she lives. I’ve been there twelve times, always by way of some back yards and completely smashed. How annoying that on the thirteenth time I’m going to see her I’m completely sober. Because ofthat I'll have to wait until it finally gets light. Until it finally dawns on my thirteenth Friday.

cases.explain: «прошлой пятницей» — after the preposition «со», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "Again, your last Friday. I see, Venya, that you are completely in the past. I see that you don’t wish to speak of the future at all."’
